Subject: Payment options for Invoice 4821 (BRL/GBP split)

Hi Karthik,

We received Invoice #4821 for the EMEA services (total GBP 98,450) but our AP team has asked whether we can: 1) pay the GBP portion via a UK-based account, and 2) settle the remaining regional fees in BRL, routed through our Brazil treasury. They want clarity on: intermediary bank fees (who bears them), whether Redwood can accept a net BRL credit (i.e., beneficiary receives net-of-fees), and if we need any tax/VAT gross-up documentation.

Can you send the wire templates and recommended payment instruction language we should provide to our banks? Also please confirm whether you can accept two separate payments referencing the same invoice and how that affects fee allocation on Redwood's side.

Thanks,
Maria Silva
Head of Treasury — Acme Health

Attachments: acme_invoice_4821.pdf (invoice PDF)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Maria Silva <maria.silva@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2028 11:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Payment options for Invoice 4821 (BRL/GBP split)

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear summary. Good news: we can accept split settlements (one GBP and one BRL) against the same invoice. A few operational notes and attached templates below.

Key points up front:
- GBP payment: send to our UK GBP nostro (bank details in attached wire_template_gbp_v2.xlsx). This should normally be received net and we will reconcile as GBP. Intermediary fees for GBP are usually borne by the sender by default (BEN vs OUR). If Acme prefers Redwood to absorb intermediaries for a single net-credit, we can discuss a gross-up credit but this requires a billing adjustment.
- BRL payment: Brazil routing frequently incurs correspondent/intermediary fees and local taxes. We cannot reliably accept a guaranteed "net-of-all-fees" BRL credit unless Acme instructs its bank to use a cover payment with a clear nostro/vostro tag; otherwise the intermediary chain will deduct fees at various hops.
- Split payments: When two payments land against the same invoice, we allocate by ledger tags you include in the payment reference; please use the exact invoice reference + portion tag (e.g., INV4821-GBP / INV4821-BRL). This prevents manual reconciliation delays.

Attached: wire_template_gbp_v2.xlsx (GBP nostro details) and a short example of how to structure BRL cover/beneficiary tags (nostro_tagging_example.txt).

Action items for Acme (recommended):
1) Send GBP to the UK nostro with OUR charges if you want Redwood to receive gross GBP.
2) For BRL, request a cover payment from your Brazilian bank using the intermediary bank listed in the example and include "INV4821-BRL" in the payment reference. If the Brazilian bank cannot send cover instructions, expect intermediary deductions and please select who bears them (sender/sender-our/beneficiary options).

Looping in Laura (finance) and Vanessa (payments ops) to confirm VAT/gross-up and any exceptions for BRL receipts.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Payments Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: wire_template_gbp_v2.xlsx, nostro_tagging_example.txt

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2028 15:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Payment options for Invoice 4821 (BRL/GBP split)

Hi Maria — quick note from Finance on VAT and collection treatment.

- VAT: The line items on Invoice 4821 are a blend of taxable and non-taxable services. Our tax team confirms the VAT treatment remains unchanged by the payment routing — the invoice is VAT-inclusive where applicable and the tax point is the invoice date. We will issue a credit note / gross-up only if Acme requests Redwood to bear intermediary bank fees as a commercial concession (we can do that, but it requires approving a customer credit and will show as a deduction on the invoice amount).
- Gross-up: If Acme asks us to guarantee a net amount (i.e., Redwood receives the full invoiced BRL after all intermediaries), we need an explicit gross-up agreement and will process an adjusted invoice reflecting the reversal/credit. We normally prefer the sender to select OUR charges if they want Redwood to receive gross.

Vanessa — please confirm operational feasibility for accepting a BRL cover payment and whether we need a separate remittance reference structure for split settlements.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
